blogs.title: The Consistency Trap: Federal Circuit Corrects TTAB's Bifurcated Similarity Analysis
blogs.description: This post analyzes the court's ruling that the Trademark Trial and Appeal Board (TTAB) cannot 'have it both ways' when applying the DuPont factors. It examines the legal error of defining services broadly to establish likelihood of confusion under the second factor (similarity of goods/services), while simultaneously defining them narrowly to exclude third-party marks under the sixth factor (crowded field analysis). The post discusses the implications for practitioners on ensuring a consistent factual record across all DuPont factors.

blogs.title: Quantifying 'Weakness': The Evidentiary Threshold for Third-Party Use
blogs.description: This post explores the tension between the TTAB's finding that nine third-party marks were insufficient to prove a mark is 'conceptually weak' and the Federal Circuit's demand for a broader scope of consideration. It discusses the 'crowded field' theory of trademark law, comparing this case to precedents like Juice Generation and Jack Wolfskin to question whether there is a predictable numerical threshold for demonstrating that a mark is entitled to a narrow scope of protection.

blogs.title: The Domino Effect: How Factor Six Collapses the Analysis of Factor One
blogs.description: This post examines the interconnectedness of the DuPont factors, specifically why the court vacated the analysis of the first factor (similarity of the marks' appearance, sound, and connotation) based solely on a legal error in the sixth factor. It analyzes the legal link between a mark's commercial strength and its overall 'commercial impression,' arguing that a finding of weakness can fundamentally alter the perceived similarity between two marks.
